description: Interactive in silico biophysical risk calculator evaluating the Host-Tumor Biophysical Index (HTBI) across post-resection solid oncology cohorts (N=3,443).
name: HTBI Research Explorer: Interactive Biophysical Risk Modeler

metadata.abstract:
Background: In solid oncology, anatomical TNM staging and somatic mutational profiling provide the cornerstone of clinical risk stratification. Nevertheless, substantial clinical heterogeneity remains unexplained: curatively resected (R0) tumors frequently recur, and targeted adjuvant therapies—such as 36-month adjuvant osimertinib in the landmark ADAURA trial—exhibit a post-discontinuation recurrence rebound where 67.9% of all relapse events cluster after planned treatment cessation without secondary gatekeeper mutations. Similarly, in desmoplastic colorectal cancer, cytotoxic chemotherapy encounters persistent micrometastatic reservoirs that evade clearance. We hypothesized that post-resection persistence and delayed relapse are modulated by the biophysical coupling between epithelial polarity integrity ("The Seed") and microenvironmental inflammatory-transport resistance ("The Soil").

Methods:

We established a multiscale biophysical reaction-diffusion continuum model integrating: 1) Spatial drug penetration across microvascular cords governed by modified cylindrical Bessel functions of the second kind (K0); 2) Interstitial transport limitations driven by elevated interstitial fluid pressure (IFP approx 20-35 mmHg) and absent functional lymphatic drainage (Delta P approx 0); 3) Plastic drug-tolerant persister (DTP) cell transitions within viable, sub-therapeutic annular niches; 4) A hereditary Volterra memory functional of residual cytotoxic immune surveillance formalizing cumulative inflammatory damage; 5) An exploratory translational metric—the Host-Tumor Biophysical Index (HTBI)—integrating histopathological polarity, stromal desmoplasia, and systemic inflammatory blood parameters (neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio [NLR] and C-reactive protein [CRP]). In accordance with REMARK reporting guidelines, the framework was evaluated across 3,443 curatively treated cancer patients across 10 certified public cohorts: Discovery Cohort (604 resected lung adenocarcinoma patients, MSKCC); Raw Blood Chemistry Cohort (1,056 curatively resected surgical patients with complete preoperative blood counts, PLOS ONE open data); Multi-Cohort Solid Epithelial Datasets (N = 1,222 clinical: TCGA-COAD, TCGA-PAAD, TCGA-ESCA, TCGA-CHOL, and GSE31210); and Proof-by-Contradiction Falsification Controls lacking solid epithelial boundaries (N = 561: TCGA-LAML, TCGA-TGCT, TCGA-SARC), anchored by the landmark CANTOS randomized trial (N = 10,061).

Findings:

In the complete-case raw laboratory cohort (N = 1,056), preoperative biophysical inflammatory tier stratified 5-year overall survival from 69.4% (Low HTBI) to 56.7% (High HTBI) (p = 3.81 x 10^-7), maintaining independent prognostic association in multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression adjusting for Pathologic TNM Stage and Histological Grade (HR = 1.43, 95% CI: 1.14-1.81, p = 0.0022; continuous multivariable HR = 2.20, p = 0.00041). In the MSKCC lung adenocarcinoma discovery cohort (N = 604), continuous HTBI conferred an adjusted HR = 2.49 (95% CI: 1.00-6.18, p = 0.050) after controlling for Pathologic TNM Stage (HR = 2.53, p < 0.0005), patient sex, and somatic EGFR mutations. 500-fold bootstrap cross-validation showed an incremental discrimination gain (Delta C-index = +0.050, p = 0.044; 2-year AUC = 0.794). In competing risks analysis (Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence), HTBI specifically stratified cancer-related recurrence (p = 0.029) while remaining unstratified for non-cancer competing mortality (p = 0.680). In proof-by-contradiction negative controls lacking solid epithelial boundaries, the model was statistically non-significant: acute myeloid leukemia (TCGA-LAML, HR = 1.28, p = 0.246), testicular germ cell tumors (TCGA-TGCT, HR = 2.33, p = 0.471), and soft-tissue sarcomas (TCGA-SARC, HR = 0.85, p = 0.413). The continuum model analytically reproduced the empirical 5.46-month median ctDNA-to-imaging lead time (transition from 10^6 to 10^8 cells, doubling time Td = 24.6 days) and simulated microenvironmental stabilization consistent with published systemic IL-1beta neutralization trials (CANTOS, HR = 0.23, p = 0.0002). Interpretation: The Host-Tumor Biophysical Index demonstrates that combining routine surgical histopathology and standard laboratory inflammatory markers with physical transport mechanics provides independent prognostic stratification across retrospective cohorts. This exploratory framework provides a mechanistic foundation for residual tumor dormancy and quantitative hypotheses for microenvironmental decompression and anti-inflammatory strategies in prospective oncological research.
metadata.title: A Multiscale Biophysical Reaction-Diffusion Framework Coupling Histological Architecture, Interstitial Transport, and Inflammatory Tension in Solid Tumors: An Exploratory In Silico and Retrospective Multi-Cohort Analysis
